item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03210","case1_error":"Uses the 12 apples Frank sold as his remaining apples, instead of subtracting them from 36.","case2_error":"Invents an additional $5,000 cost absent from the question and subtracts it from revenue.","reason":"The first confuses the removed portion with the remainder; the second introduces an unsupported expense.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03211","case1_error":"Derives sales counts from inventory divided by price, contradicts the given $60 revenue, and counts all inventory again as paired sales.","case2_error":"Invents an additional $5,000 cost absent from the question and subtracts it from revenue.","reason":"The first uses invalid sales relations and double-counts inventory; the second adds a fabricated expense.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03212","case1_error":"Counts only two houses instead of Zion’s house plus his two friends’ houses; equal house areas are also unstated.","case2_error":"Divides total area by six as though all rooms were equal, despite the living room occupying three ordinary-room equivalents.","reason":"Similar shapes do not establish equal areas, leaving the first question materially underdetermined. The second clearly mishandles unequal room sizes.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J03213","case1_error":"Divides days by words instead of words by days, producing the reciprocal of the requested rate.","case2_error":"Uses the daily 500-calorie deficit instead of the 4,000-calorie requirement per pound to calculate the total required deficit.","reason":"The first reverses a rate’s numerator and denominator; the second substitutes the wrong quantity into the weight-to-calories conversion.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03214","case1_error":"Doubles the second country’s duration for the third country instead of doubling the first country’s duration for both.","case2_error":"Adds only one three-second elevator stop despite stops occurring on every floor, causing the slower traveler to be misidentified.","reason":"The first applies a multiplier to the wrong baseline; the second counts a recurring delay only once.","judgment":"different"}]}
